summary: Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Exeter (1987–1990). He held posts at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and Nottingham Trent University from 1995, where he served as Professor of Gambling Studies around 1995.

Mark Juergensmeyer, a scholar in religious studies and Indology, studied at the University of Illinois System, Columbia University's SIPA, and Union Theological Seminary. Around 1993, he became professor of sociology and religious studies and Director of Global and International Studies at UC Santa Barbara.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held an assistant professorship at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and served as Associate Professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006).
Mark Owen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Leeds under doctoral supervisors Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Indologist Mark S. G. Dyczkowski earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford (~1975–1980) under Richard Gombrich. He also studied under traditional teachers Lakshman Joo (~1970–1991) and Kedar Raj Rajopadhyaya.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught at Illinois State University (~1979–2007; Emeritus Professor ~2007) and was later an Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Seoul National University (attested 2011–2014).

Mark Singleton, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge and studied under Lakshmi Tatacharya. In 2020, he was attested as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London.

Mark T. Unno, a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar, studied at Oberlin College (~1977–1981) and Stanford University. He held positions at Brown University and at the University of Oregon (~1998) as Assistant Professor of East Asian Religions.

Mark Tatz (1946–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz, studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Appey Rinpoche, and served as Professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 1988).

Mark Teeuwen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1991–1996). Around 1999, he was appointed Professor of Japanese Studies at the University of Oslo.

Markus Viehbeck, a specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD from the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at the University of Vienna (attested 2011) and Heidelberg University as a project researcher.

Marsha Weidner, a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley. She was an assistant professor of art history at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and Professor of the History of Art at the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at New York University (~1965–1969) and Harvard University (~1969–1975). She held academic posts at Harvard (~1975–1983), Brown University (~1984–1995), and the University of Chicago (~1995).
Martin Baumann is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He joined the University of Lucerne in 2001, where he became Professor of Religious Studies around that year.

Martin Brauen is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied at the University of Zurich and the University of Delhi, alongside multiple traditional teachers. He served as Konservator at the University of Zurich from ~1975 to 2008.

Martin Collcutt, a scholar of Japanology and history, studied at Cambridge and earned his PhD at Harvard. He taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo (1963–1969), and later served as Director of East Asian Studies at Princeton (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and studied at Kyoto. His career includes posts at Hamburg, Shandong University, the University of Göttingen, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Ryukoku University.

Martin Haug (1827–1876), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Tübingen and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (~1859–1866), and was Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Munich (~1868–1876).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who completed his Magisterarbeit and PhD at the University of Freiburg under Eva Tichy and others. He held a post at the University of Jena around 2013.

Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology who studied at Cornell University (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1964–1971). He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1970–1994) and Harvard University (~2000–2015).
